title: Max Out
summary: Fly a cargo drone that cuts, folds and fits: write the load or cost as f(x), solve f′(x) = 0 and prove the extreme with f″.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Using a constraint to remove a variable
learningOutcome: The student can turn a word problem into a function of one variable, find the critical point, reject roots that are impossible, and confirm a maximum or minimum with the second derivative.

levels.title: Fold the box
levels.adds: Baseline: the volume of an open box is V(x) = x(a − 2x)(b − 2x); solve V′ = 0 and reject the cut that is too big (Ex 6.3 Q17, Q18; Example 36).
hints: Cutting x from each corner leaves a base of (a − 2x) by (b − 2x) and a height of x.
Expand V, differentiate and solve V′ = 0. You get two roots; one cannot be a real cut.
A cut cannot be more than half the shorter side.

levels.title: Least metal and cost
levels.adds: New: minimise instead of maximise, using the fixed volume to remove one variable and f″ > 0 to confirm (Ex 6.3 Q20, Q21; Misc Q6).
hints: The volume is fixed, so h (or the second side) can be written in terms of x.
Write the metal or the cost as a function of x alone, then differentiate.
At the answer, f″ is positive: that is a minimum.

levels.title: Fit one inside another
levels.adds: New: the constraint comes from a second shape, using Pythagoras or similar triangles (Ex 6.3 Q23; Misc Q12, Q15; Example 26).
hints: Cone in a sphere: the base radius r satisfies r² = h(2R − h).
Cylinder in a cone: similar triangles give r in terms of h.
Read what is being maximised: volume and curved surface peak at different heights.

levels.title: The rescue line
levels.adds: Harder: minimise the distance from a point to a curve, working with D² to avoid the square root (Example 29; Ex 6.3 Q27).
hints: Write D² = (x − p)² + y², with y given by the cable’s equation.
D² and D are smallest at the same x, so differentiate D².
The derivative of D² is a cubic in x; look for a whole-number root.

misconceptions: f′(x) = 0 always gives the answer without checking it
Every root of f′ is a valid setting
Maximum volume and maximum surface are at the same setting
